1	import AppKit
2	import UniformTypeIdentifiers
3	
4	/// File ▸ Import Captions… — a SubRip (`.srt`) file becomes TEXT CLIPS on a
5	/// track of their own (road map Phase 6, "SRT captions").
6	///
7	/// **Why text clips rather than a caption model.** Burn-in then costs
8	/// nothing: a text clip already draws through `LayerRenderers`, already
9	/// composites through `Compositor.metal` and already exports through the
10	/// same pass, so an imported caption shows up in the preview, in
11	/// `render_frame` and in the written movie without one line of export code.
12	/// It also leaves every caption editable with the tools that already exist —
13	/// drag one to retime it, select the lot and restyle them in the Text pane —
14	/// which a parallel caption model would have had to earn back one command at
15	/// a time. The cost is that captions are not a switchable soft-subtitle
16	/// track; §1 does not ask for one.
17	///
18	/// **The grammar.** SubRip is blocks separated by blank lines:
19	///
20	/// ```
21	/// 1
22	/// 00:00:04,120 --> 00:00:06,480
23	/// Two lines of
24	/// caption text.
25	/// ```
26	///
27	/// Handled here, because every one of them is in files people actually have:
28	/// a UTF-8 BOM, CRLF or bare-CR line endings, a missing index line, the
29	/// comma decimal separator (and the dot some tools write instead), the
30	/// `HH:MM:SS` / `MM:SS` shorthands, cue-position settings trailing the end
31	/// timestamp, `<i>`/`<b>`/`<font>` inline tags and `{\an8}` overrides, the
32	/// handful of HTML entities, and text encoded as UTF-16 or Windows-1252
33	/// rather than UTF-8.
34	///
35	/// **Malformed entries are reported, never silently dropped** — the parser
36	/// keeps the line number of every block it refused and the caller shows
37	/// them. A caption file half of which vanished without a word is worse than
38	/// one that did not import.
39	///
40	/// Times snap to the canvas frame grid like every other time in this app
41	/// (spec §5.1), which is also why a caption may end up one frame shorter
42	/// than the file says.
43	///
44	/// **What is here is the SubRip grammar and nothing else.** Everything from
45	/// the frame grid onwards — snapping, the overlap trim, the Caption preset,
46	/// the new front-most track and the probe that learns the new clips' ids —
47	/// is `CaptionLayout`, so `Transcriber.swift` lays a transcript out exactly
48	/// as a file is laid out. `plan(for:in:track:)` below is the whole seam:
49	/// read, parse, hand the cues over, rewrap the error with the file's name.
50	enum CaptionImporter {
51	
52	    // MARK: - What a file parses into
53	
54	    /// One cue as WRITTEN — before the frame grid, before overlap fixing.
55	    struct Cue: Equatable {
56	        /// The file's own numbering, when the block carried one. Kept only
57	        /// so a message can name the entry the way the file does.
58	        let index: Int?
59	        /// 1-based line of the block's timing line, for problem messages.
60	        let line: Int
61	        let start: Ticks
62	        let end: Ticks
63	        let text: String
64	    }
65	
66	    /// A block the parser refused, or a cue placement gave up on — the
67	    /// shared type, whose `tag` this file always spells `"line <n>"`, so
68	    /// `description` reads `"line 12: no caption text"` exactly as it did
69	    /// when the line number was a field of its own.
70	    typealias Problem = CaptionLayout.Problem
71	
72	    /// What an import will do, before anything is applied. The layout's, so
73	    /// a transcript and a file produce the same shape of answer.
74	    typealias Plan = CaptionLayout.Plan
75	
76	    /// A refusal naming the line it came from.
77	    private static func problem(line: Int, reason: String) -> Problem {
78	        Problem(tag: "line \(line)", reason: reason)
79	    }
80	
81	    struct ParsedFile: Equatable {
82	        let cues: [Cue]
83	        let problems: [Problem]
84	    }
85	
86	    /// What one block parsed to. `Result` would want `Problem` to conform to
87	    /// `Error`, and a problem is something to REPORT, not something to
88	    /// throw — the parser keeps going past every one of them.
89	    private enum Block {
90	        case cue(Cue)
91	        case problem(Problem)
92	    }
93	
94	    /// Why an import produced nothing. Every case carries the file, because
95	    /// an agent may have named a path the user never saw — which is also why
96	    /// `CaptionLayout.LayoutError`, whose producer is not always a file, is
97	    /// caught and rewrapped into these rather than thrown through.
98	    enum CaptionError: LocalizedError {
99	        case unreadable(URL)
100	        case noCues(URL, [Problem])
101	        case refused(URL)
102	        case tooMany(URL, cues: Int, room: Int)
103	
104	        var errorDescription: String? {
105	            switch self {
106	            case .unreadable(let url):
107	                return "“\(url.lastPathComponent)” could not be read as text."
108	            case .noCues(let url, let problems):
109	                let detail = problems.prefix(3).map { $0.description }.joined(separator: "; ")
110	                return "No captions could be read from “\(url.lastPathComponent)”."
111	                    + (detail.isEmpty ? "" : " \(detail).")
112	            case .refused(let url):
113	                return "The captions in “\(url.lastPathComponent)” could not be placed on the "
114	                    + "timeline."
115	            case .tooMany(let url, let cues, let room):
116	                return "“\(url.lastPathComponent)” holds \(cues) captions, more than this "
117	                    + "project has room for: \(room) more clip\(room == 1 ? "" : "s") would "
118	                    + "fit, out of \(Int(RC_MAX_CLIPS))."
119	            }
120	        }
121	    }
122	
123	    // MARK: - Reading
124	
125	    /// The types File ▸ Import Captions… offers. `.srt` is not a registered
126	    /// system type, so `UTType(filenameExtension:)` mints the same dynamic
127	    /// type a `.srt` file on disk is itself given — which is what makes the
128	    /// filter match it — and the text types ride along for a caption file
129	    /// some other app has claimed.
130	    static var contentTypes: [UTType] {
131	        var types: [UTType] = [.plainText, .text]
132	        if let srt = UTType(filenameExtension: "srt") { types.insert(srt, at: 0) }
133	        return types
134	    }
135	
136	    /// The file's text. UTF-8 first (what every modern tool writes), then
137	    /// UTF-16 for a file with a wide BOM, then the two single-byte encodings
138	    /// a subtitle file off a DVD rip is likely to be in. Latin-1 maps all
139	    /// 256 bytes, so the last arm never fails on a file that exists —
140	    /// mojibake is a better answer here than a refusal, since the timing
141	    /// lines are ASCII either way.
142	    static func text(of url: URL) throws -> String {
143	        guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url) else { throw CaptionError.unreadable(url) }
144	        for encoding in [String.Encoding.utf8, .utf16, .windowsCP1252, .isoLatin1] {
145	            if let text = String(data: data, encoding: encoding) { return text }
146	        }
147	        throw CaptionError.unreadable(url)
148	    }
149	
150	    // MARK: - Parsing
151	
152	    /// Splits the file into blocks on blank lines and parses each one. A
153	    /// block that is not a cue becomes a `Problem` naming its first line;
154	    /// parsing never stops at the first bad block, because one broken entry
155	    /// in a thousand-line file must not cost the other 999.
156	    static func parse(_ raw: String) -> ParsedFile {
157	        let lines = normalized(raw).components(separatedBy: "\n")
158	        var cues: [Cue] = []
159	        var problems: [Problem] = []
160	        var index = 0
161	        while index < lines.count {
162	            while index < lines.count, isBlank(lines[index]) { index += 1 }
163	            guard index < lines.count else { break }
164	            let first = index
165	            var block: [String] = []
166	            while index < lines.count, !isBlank(lines[index]) {
167	                block.append(lines[index])
168	                index += 1
169	            }
170	            switch cue(from: block, firstLine: first + 1) {
171	            case .cue(let cue): cues.append(cue)
172	            case .problem(let problem): problems.append(problem)
173	            }
174	        }
175	        return ParsedFile(cues: cues, problems: problems)
176	    }
177	
178	    /// One block. The timing line is found by searching for `-->` rather
179	    /// than by counting lines, which is what makes the index line optional
180	    /// — plenty of tools omit it.
181	    private static func cue(from block: [String], firstLine: Int) -> Block {
182	        guard let offset = block.firstIndex(where: { $0.contains("-->") }) else {
183	            return .problem(
184	                problem(line: firstLine, reason: "no “-->” timing line in this entry"))
185	        }
186	        let timingLine = firstLine + offset
187	        if offset > 1 {
188	            return .problem(
189	                problem(line: firstLine, reason: "\(offset) lines before the timing line"))
190	        }
191	        let number = offset == 1 ? Int(block[0].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)) : nil
192	
193	        let halves = block[offset].components(separatedBy: "-->")
194	        guard halves.count == 2 else {
195	            return .problem(problem(line: timingLine, reason: "two “-->” in one timing line"))
196	        }
197	        guard let start = ticks(fromTimestamp: halves[0]) else {
198	            return .problem(
199	                problem(
200	                    line: timingLine,
201	                    reason: "“\(trimmed(halves[0]))” is not a HH:MM:SS,mmm time"))
202	        }
203	        guard let end = ticks(fromTimestamp: halves[1]) else {
204	            return .problem(
205	                problem(
206	                    line: timingLine,
207	                    reason: "“\(trimmed(halves[1]))” is not a HH:MM:SS,mmm time"))
208	        }
209	        guard end > start else {
210	            return .problem(problem(line: timingLine, reason: "ends at or before it starts"))
211	        }
212	
213	        let body = block.dropFirst(offset + 1).map { plainText($0) }
214	        let text = body.joined(separator: "\n").trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
215	        guard !text.isEmpty else {
216	            return .problem(problem(line: timingLine, reason: "no caption text"))
217	        }
218	        return .cue(Cue(index: number, line: timingLine, start: start, end: end, text: text))
219	    }
220	
221	    /// One SubRip timestamp. Accepts `HH:MM:SS,mmm`, the dot some tools
222	    /// write instead of the comma, the `MM:SS` and `SS` shorthands, and any
223	    /// number of fraction digits; ignores whatever follows the timestamp,
224	    /// which is where SubRip's optional position settings (`X1:… X2:…`)
225	    /// live. Arithmetic is integer throughout so a timestamp lands on the
226	    /// tick the file meant rather than near it.
227	    static func ticks(fromTimestamp text: String) -> Ticks? {
228	        guard let token = text.split(whereSeparator: { $0 == " " || $0 == "\t" }).first
229	        else { return nil }
230	        let parts = token.replacingOccurrences(of: ",", with: ".")
231	            .split(separator: ":", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)
232	        guard parts.count >= 1, parts.count <= 3 else { return nil }
233	
234	        var seconds: Ticks = 0
235	        for part in parts.dropLast() {
236	            guard let value = wholeNumber(part) else { return nil }
237	            seconds = seconds * 60 + value
238	        }
239	        guard let lastPart = parts.last else { return nil }
240	        let halves = lastPart.split(separator: ".", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)
241	        guard halves.count <= 2, let whole = wholeNumber(halves[0]) else { return nil }
242	        seconds = seconds * 60 + whole
243	        // A day of captions is 86 400 s; the cap is only here so the
244	        // multiplication below cannot overflow on a garbage timestamp.
245	        guard seconds >= 0, seconds <= 1_000_000 else { return nil }
246	
247	        var total = seconds * ReelTime.perSecond
248	        if halves.count == 2 {
249	            let digits = halves[1]
250	            guard digits.count <= 9, let value = wholeNumber(digits) else { return nil }
251	            var scale: Ticks = 1
252	            for _ in 0..<digits.count { scale *= 10 }
253	            total += (ReelTime.perSecond * value + scale / 2) / scale
254	        }
255	        return total
256	    }
257	
258	    /// A run of ASCII digits as a number — `Int64.init` would also accept a
259	    /// sign and Unicode digits, neither of which is a timestamp.
260	    private static func wholeNumber(_ text: Substring) -> Ticks? {
261	        guard !text.isEmpty, text.count <= 18,
262	              text.allSatisfy({ $0.isASCII && $0.isNumber })
263	        else { return nil }
264	        return Ticks(text)
265	    }
266	
267	    /// Strips the inline markup SubRip carries — `<i>`, `<b>`, `<u>`,
268	    /// `<font …>` and the ASS `{\an8}` overrides — and decodes the entities
269	    /// that come with it. The model has one plain string per text clip
270	    /// (spec §5.2), so markup that cannot be honoured is removed rather than
271	    /// shown as angle brackets on the canvas.
272	    private static func plainText(_ raw: String) -> String {
273	        var out = ""
274	        var index = raw.startIndex
275	        while index < raw.endIndex {
276	            let character = raw[index]
277	            let rest = raw[raw.index(after: index)...]
278	            if character == "<", let close = rest.firstIndex(of: ">"),
279	               looksLikeTag(rest[rest.startIndex..<close]) {
280	                index = raw.index(after: close)
281	                continue
282	            }
283	            if character == "{", let close = rest.firstIndex(of: "}"),
284	               rest[rest.startIndex..<close].first == "\\" {
285	                index = raw.index(after: close)
286	                continue
287	            }
288	            out.append(character)
289	            index = raw.index(after: index)
290	        }
291	        return decodeEntities(out)
292	    }
293	
294	    /// `<i>` and `</font>` are markup; `<<` and `a < b` are text. The test
295	    /// is the one HTML itself uses: a tag opens with a letter, or with a
296	    /// slash and a letter.
297	    private static func looksLikeTag(_ body: Substring) -> Bool {
298	        guard let first = body.first else { return false }
299	        if first == "/" { return body.dropFirst().first?.isLetter == true }
300	        return first.isLetter
301	    }
302	
303	    /// `&` last, or every other decoded entity would be decoded twice.
304	    private static func decodeEntities(_ text: String) -> String {
305	        guard text.contains("&") else { return text }
306	        var out = text
307	        for (entity, character) in [
308	            ("<", "<"), (">", ">"), (""", "\""), ("'", "'"),
309	            ("'", "'"), (" ", " "), ("&", "&"),
310	        ] {
311	            out = out.replacingOccurrences(of: entity, with: character)
312	        }
313	        return out
314	    }
315	
316	    /// A leading BOM survives `String(data:encoding:.utf8)` as U+FEFF, and
317	    /// left in place it makes the first block's index line unparseable.
318	    private static func normalized(_ raw: String) -> String {
319	        raw.replacingOccurrences(of: "\u{FEFF}", with: "")
320	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "\r\n", with: "\n")
321	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "\r", with: "\n")
322	    }
323	
324	    private static func isBlank(_ line: String) -> Bool {
325	        line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty
326	    }
327	
328	    private static func trimmed(_ text: String) -> String {
329	        text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
330	    }
331	
332	    // MARK: - Placement
333	
334	    /// Everything an import will do, computed against `project` and applied
335	    /// by nobody: the UI commits it through `ProjectDocument`, the agent
336	    /// through `AgentServer.editResult`.
337	    ///
338	    /// The whole of the placement is `CaptionLayout.place` — this is the
339	    /// SubRip half handing its cues over, and the file name being put back
340	    /// into the refusals so the alert and the tool's error string say which
341	    /// file they are about.
342	    ///
343	    /// `track` places on an existing track; absent, the captions get a new
344	    /// front-most track of their own, which is the only placement that can
345	    /// never be refused by the overlap rule.
346	    static func plan(for url: URL, in project: ReelProject, track: UInt32? = nil) throws -> Plan {
347	        let parsed = parse(try text(of: url))
348	        guard !parsed.cues.isEmpty else {
349	            throw CaptionError.noCues(url, parsed.problems)
350	        }
351	        let cues = parsed.cues.map {
352	            CaptionLayout.Cue(start: $0.start, end: $0.end, text: $0.text, tag: "line \($0.line)")
353	        }
354	        do {
355	            return try CaptionLayout.place(
356	                cues, problems: parsed.problems, in: project, track: track)
357	        } catch let error as CaptionLayout.LayoutError {
358	            switch error {
359	            case .noCues(let problems): throw CaptionError.noCues(url, problems)
360	            case .refused: throw CaptionError.refused(url)
361	            case .tooMany(let cues, let room):
362	                throw CaptionError.tooMany(url, cues: cues, room: room)
363	            }
364	        }
365	    }
366	}

370	/// File ▸ Import Captions…, mirrored by the agent's `import_captions`
371	/// (`AgentServer+Media.swift`).
372	extension EditorViewController {
373	
374	    /// The open panel, then the import. Both the panel's completion and the
375	    /// alert that follows it are OFF-EVENT, which is why the edit goes
376	    /// through `performGroupedEdit` (app/CLAUDE.md's undo pitfall).
377	    func importCaptionsCommand() {
378	        guard let document = document, let window = view.window else {
379	            NSSound.beep()
380	            return
381	        }
382	        let panel = NSOpenPanel()
383	        panel.allowsMultipleSelection = false
384	        panel.canChooseDirectories = false
385	        panel.allowedContentTypes = CaptionImporter.contentTypes
386	        panel.message = "Choose a SubRip (.srt) caption file."
387	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak self] response in
388	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
389	            self?.importCaptions(from: url, into: document, in: window)
390	        }
391	    }
392	
393	    private func importCaptions(from url: URL, into document: ProjectDocument, in window: NSWindow)
394	    {
395	        let plan: CaptionImporter.Plan
396	        do {
397	            // **The EDITED project, not the document.** A caption plan
398	            // measures a placement — the frame grid, the overlap trim, the
399	            // new front-most track — and road map 2's phase 9 addresses the
400	            // ops it produces to whatever nest is open. Reading the document
401	            // here and writing into the nest there is one gesture computing
402	            // against one container and landing in another, which is the
403	            // shape `SilenceDetector` and `AudioNormalize` were moved off
404	            // in the same phase. A producer reads the container it writes.
405	            plan = try CaptionImporter.plan(for: url, in: document.editedProject)
406	        } catch {
407	            let alert = NSAlert(error: error)
408	            alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
409	            return
410	        }
411	        document.performGroupedEdit("Import Captions", plan.ops)
412	        guard !plan.report.isEmpty else { return }
413	        let alert = NSAlert()
414	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
415	        alert.messageText =
416	            "Imported \(plan.clips) caption\(plan.clips == 1 ? "" : "s") from "
417	            + "“\(url.lastPathComponent)”."
418	        alert.informativeText = plan.report
419	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "OK")
420	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
421	    }
422	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),

  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an

  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is

  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE

- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an

  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,

  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror

  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

4	/// File ▸ Import Captions… — a SubRip (`.srt`) file becomes TEXT CLIPS on a
5	/// track of their own (road map Phase 6, "SRT captions").
6	///
7	/// **Why text clips rather than a caption model.** Burn-in then costs
8	/// nothing: a text clip already draws through `LayerRenderers`, already
9	/// composites through `Compositor.metal` and already exports through the
10	/// same pass, so an imported caption shows up in the preview, in
11	/// `render_frame` and in the written movie without one line of export code.
12	/// It also leaves every caption editable with the tools that already exist —
13	/// drag one to retime it, select the lot and restyle them in the Text pane —
14	/// which a parallel caption model would have had to earn back one command at
15	/// a time. The cost is that captions are not a switchable soft-subtitle
16	/// track; §1 does not ask for one.
17	///
18	/// **The grammar.** SubRip is blocks separated by blank lines:
19	///
20	/// ```
21	/// 1
22	/// 00:00:04,120 --> 00:00:06,480
23	/// Two lines of
24	/// caption text.
25	/// ```
26	///
27	/// Handled here, because every one of them is in files people actually have:
28	/// a UTF-8 BOM, CRLF or bare-CR line endings, a missing index line, the
29	/// comma decimal separator (and the dot some tools write instead), the
30	/// `HH:MM:SS` / `MM:SS` shorthands, cue-position settings trailing the end
31	/// timestamp, `<i>`/`<b>`/`<font>` inline tags and `{\an8}` overrides, the
32	/// handful of HTML entities, and text encoded as UTF-16 or Windows-1252
33	/// rather than UTF-8.
34	///
35	/// **Malformed entries are reported, never silently dropped** — the parser
36	/// keeps the line number of every block it refused and the caller shows
37	/// them. A caption file half of which vanished without a word is worse than
38	/// one that did not import.
39	///
40	/// Times snap to the canvas frame grid like every other time in this app
41	/// (spec §5.1), which is also why a caption may end up one frame shorter
42	/// than the file says.
43	///
44	/// **What is here is the SubRip grammar and nothing else.** Everything from
45	/// the frame grid onwards — snapping, the overlap trim, the Caption preset,
46	/// the new front-most track and the probe that learns the new clips' ids —
47	/// is `CaptionLayout`, so `Transcriber.swift` lays a transcript out exactly
48	/// as a file is laid out. `plan(for:in:track:)` below is the whole seam:
49	/// read, parse, hand the cues over, rewrap the error with the file's name.
50	enum CaptionImporter {
51	
52	    // MARK: - What a file parses into
53	
54	    /// One cue as WRITTEN — before the frame grid, before overlap fixing.
55	    struct Cue: Equatable {
56	        /// The file's own numbering, when the block carried one. Kept only
57	        /// so a message can name the entry the way the file does.
58	        let index: Int?
59	        /// 1-based line of the block's timing line, for problem messages.
60	        let line: Int
61	        let start: Ticks
62	        let end: Ticks
63	        let text: String
64	    }
65	
66	    /// A block the parser refused, or a cue placement gave up on — the
67	    /// shared type, whose `tag` this file always spells `"line <n>"`, so
68	    /// `description` reads `"line 12: no caption text"` exactly as it did
69	    /// when the line number was a field of its own.
70	    typealias Problem = CaptionLayout.Problem
71	
72	    /// What an import will do, before anything is applied. The layout's, so
73	    /// a transcript and a file produce the same shape of answer.
74	    typealias Plan = CaptionLayout.Plan
75	
76	    /// A refusal naming the line it came from.
77	    private static func problem(line: Int, reason: String) -> Problem {
78	        Problem(tag: "line \(line)", reason: reason)
79	    }
80	
81	    struct ParsedFile: Equatable {
82	        let cues: [Cue]
83	        let problems: [Problem]
84	    }
85	
86	    /// What one block parsed to. `Result` would want `Problem` to conform to
87	    /// `Error`, and a problem is something to REPORT, not something to
88	    /// throw — the parser keeps going past every one of them.
89	    private enum Block {
90	        case cue(Cue)
91	        case problem(Problem)
92	    }
93	
94	    /// Why an import produced nothing. Every case carries the file, because
95	    /// an agent may have named a path the user never saw — which is also why
96	    /// `CaptionLayout.LayoutError`, whose producer is not always a file, is
97	    /// caught and rewrapped into these rather than thrown through.
98	    enum CaptionError: LocalizedError {
99	        case unreadable(URL)
100	        case noCues(URL, [Problem])
101	        case refused(URL)
102	        case tooMany(URL, cues: Int, room: Int)
103	
104	        var errorDescription: String? {
105	            switch self {
106	            case .unreadable(let url):
107	                return "“\(url.lastPathComponent)” could not be read as text."
108	            case .noCues(let url, let problems):
109	                let detail = problems.prefix(3).map { $0.description }.joined(separator: "; ")
110	                return "No captions could be read from “\(url.lastPathComponent)”."
111	                    + (detail.isEmpty ? "" : " \(detail).")
112	            case .refused(let url):
113	                return "The captions in “\(url.lastPathComponent)” could not be placed on the "
114	                    + "timeline."
115	            case .tooMany(let url, let cues, let room):
116	                return "“\(url.lastPathComponent)” holds \(cues) captions, more than this "
117	                    + "project has room for: \(room) more clip\(room == 1 ? "" : "s") would "
118	                    + "fit, out of \(Int(RC_MAX_CLIPS))."
119	            }
120	        }
121	    }
122	
123	    // MARK: - Reading
124	
125	    /// The types File ▸ Import Captions… offers. `.srt` is not a registered
126	    /// system type, so `UTType(filenameExtension:)` mints the same dynamic
127	    /// type a `.srt` file on disk is itself given — which is what makes the
128	    /// filter match it — and the text types ride along for a caption file
129	    /// some other app has claimed.
130	    static var contentTypes: [UTType] {
131	        var types: [UTType] = [.plainText, .text]
132	        if let srt = UTType(filenameExtension: "srt") { types.insert(srt, at: 0) }
133	        return types
134	    }
135	
136	    /// The file's text. UTF-8 first (what every modern tool writes), then
137	    /// UTF-16 for a file with a wide BOM, then the two single-byte encodings
138	    /// a subtitle file off a DVD rip is likely to be in. Latin-1 maps all
139	    /// 256 bytes, so the last arm never fails on a file that exists —
140	    /// mojibake is a better answer here than a refusal, since the timing
141	    /// lines are ASCII either way.
142	    static func text(of url: URL) throws -> String {
143	        guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url) else { throw CaptionError.unreadable(url) }
144	        for encoding in [String.Encoding.utf8, .utf16, .windowsCP1252, .isoLatin1] {
145	            if let text = String(data: data, encoding: encoding) { return text }
146	        }
147	        throw CaptionError.unreadable(url)
148	    }
149	
150	    // MARK: - Parsing
151	
152	    /// Splits the file into blocks on blank lines and parses each one. A
153	    /// block that is not a cue becomes a `Problem` naming its first line;
154	    /// parsing never stops at the first bad block, because one broken entry
155	    /// in a thousand-line file must not cost the other 999.
156	    static func parse(_ raw: String) -> ParsedFile {
157	        let lines = normalized(raw).components(separatedBy: "\n")
158	        var cues: [Cue] = []
159	        var problems: [Problem] = []
160	        var index = 0
161	        while index < lines.count {
162	            while index < lines.count, isBlank(lines[index]) { index += 1 }
163	            guard index < lines.count else { break }
164	            let first = index
165	            var block: [String] = []
166	            while index < lines.count, !isBlank(lines[index]) {
167	                block.append(lines[index])
168	                index += 1
169	            }
170	            switch cue(from: block, firstLine: first + 1) {
171	            case .cue(let cue): cues.append(cue)
172	            case .problem(let problem): problems.append(problem)
173	            }
174	        }
175	        return ParsedFile(cues: cues, problems: problems)
176	    }
177	
178	    /// One block. The timing line is found by searching for `-->` rather
179	    /// than by counting lines, which is what makes the index line optional
180	    /// — plenty of tools omit it.
181	    private static func cue(from block: [String], firstLine: Int) -> Block {
182	        guard let offset = block.firstIndex(where: { $0.contains("-->") }) else {
183	            return .problem(
184	                problem(line: firstLine, reason: "no “-->” timing line in this entry"))
185	        }
186	        let timingLine = firstLine + offset
187	        if offset > 1 {
188	            return .problem(
189	                problem(line: firstLine, reason: "\(offset) lines before the timing line"))
190	        }
191	        let number = offset == 1 ? Int(block[0].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)) : nil
192	
193	        let halves = block[offset].components(separatedBy: "-->")
194	        guard halves.count == 2 else {
195	            return .problem(problem(line: timingLine, reason: "two “-->” in one timing line"))
196	        }
197	        guard let start = ticks(fromTimestamp: halves[0]) else {
198	            return .problem(
199	                problem(
200	                    line: timingLine,
201	                    reason: "“\(trimmed(halves[0]))” is not a HH:MM:SS,mmm time"))
202	        }
203	        guard let end = ticks(fromTimestamp: halves[1]) else {
204	            return .problem(
205	                problem(
206	                    line: timingLine,
207	                    reason: "“\(trimmed(halves[1]))” is not a HH:MM:SS,mmm time"))
208	        }
209	        guard end > start else {
210	            return .problem(problem(line: timingLine, reason: "ends at or before it starts"))
211	        }
212	
213	        let body = block.dropFirst(offset + 1).map { plainText($0) }
214	        let text = body.joined(separator: "\n").trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
215	        guard !text.isEmpty else {
216	            return .problem(problem(line: timingLine, reason: "no caption text"))
217	        }
218	        return .cue(Cue(index: number, line: timingLine, start: start, end: end, text: text))
219	    }
220	
221	    /// One SubRip timestamp. Accepts `HH:MM:SS,mmm`, the dot some tools
222	    /// write instead of the comma, the `MM:SS` and `SS` shorthands, and any
223	    /// number of fraction digits; ignores whatever follows the timestamp,
224	    /// which is where SubRip's optional position settings (`X1:… X2:…`)
225	    /// live. Arithmetic is integer throughout so a timestamp lands on the
226	    /// tick the file meant rather than near it.
227	    static func ticks(fromTimestamp text: String) -> Ticks? {
228	        guard let token = text.split(whereSeparator: { $0 == " " || $0 == "\t" }).first
229	        else { return nil }
230	        let parts = token.replacingOccurrences(of: ",", with: ".")
231	            .split(separator: ":", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)
232	        guard parts.count >= 1, parts.count <= 3 else { return nil }
233	
234	        var seconds: Ticks = 0
235	        for part in parts.dropLast() {
236	            guard let value = wholeNumber(part) else { return nil }
237	            seconds = seconds * 60 + value
238	        }
239	        guard let lastPart = parts.last else { return nil }
240	        let halves = lastPart.split(separator: ".", omittingEmptySubsequences: false)
241	        guard halves.count <= 2, let whole = wholeNumber(halves[0]) else { return nil }
242	        seconds = seconds * 60 + whole
243	        // A day of captions is 86 400 s; the cap is only here so the
244	        // multiplication below cannot overflow on a garbage timestamp.
245	        guard seconds >= 0, seconds <= 1_000_000 else { return nil }
246	
247	        var total = seconds * ReelTime.perSecond
248	        if halves.count == 2 {
249	            let digits = halves[1]
250	            guard digits.count <= 9, let value = wholeNumber(digits) else { return nil }
251	            var scale: Ticks = 1
252	            for _ in 0..<digits.count { scale *= 10 }
253	            total += (ReelTime.perSecond * value + scale / 2) / scale
254	        }
255	        return total
256	    }
257	
258	    /// A run of ASCII digits as a number — `Int64.init` would also accept a
259	    /// sign and Unicode digits, neither of which is a timestamp.
260	    private static func wholeNumber(_ text: Substring) -> Ticks? {
261	        guard !text.isEmpty, text.count <= 18,
262	              text.allSatisfy({ $0.isASCII && $0.isNumber })
263	        else { return nil }
264	        return Ticks(text)
265	    }
266	
267	    /// Strips the inline markup SubRip carries — `<i>`, `<b>`, `<u>`,
268	    /// `<font …>` and the ASS `{\an8}` overrides — and decodes the entities
269	    /// that come with it. The model has one plain string per text clip
270	    /// (spec §5.2), so markup that cannot be honoured is removed rather than
271	    /// shown as angle brackets on the canvas.
272	    private static func plainText(_ raw: String) -> String {
273	        var out = ""
274	        var index = raw.startIndex
275	        while index < raw.endIndex {
276	            let character = raw[index]
277	            let rest = raw[raw.index(after: index)...]
278	            if character == "<", let close = rest.firstIndex(of: ">"),
279	               looksLikeTag(rest[rest.startIndex..<close]) {
280	                index = raw.index(after: close)
281	                continue
282	            }
283	            if character == "{", let close = rest.firstIndex(of: "}"),
284	               rest[rest.startIndex..<close].first == "\\" {
285	                index = raw.index(after: close)
286	                continue
287	            }
288	            out.append(character)
289	            index = raw.index(after: index)
290	        }
291	        return decodeEntities(out)
292	    }
293	
294	    /// `<i>` and `</font>` are markup; `<<` and `a < b` are text. The test
295	    /// is the one HTML itself uses: a tag opens with a letter, or with a
296	    /// slash and a letter.
297	    private static func looksLikeTag(_ body: Substring) -> Bool {
298	        guard let first = body.first else { return false }
299	        if first == "/" { return body.dropFirst().first?.isLetter == true }
300	        return first.isLetter
301	    }
302	
303	    /// `&` last, or every other decoded entity would be decoded twice.
304	    private static func decodeEntities(_ text: String) -> String {
305	        guard text.contains("&") else { return text }
306	        var out = text
307	        for (entity, character) in [
308	            ("<", "<"), (">", ">"), (""", "\""), ("'", "'"),
309	            ("'", "'"), (" ", " "), ("&", "&"),
310	        ] {
311	            out = out.replacingOccurrences(of: entity, with: character)
312	        }
313	        return out
314	    }
315	
316	    /// A leading BOM survives `String(data:encoding:.utf8)` as U+FEFF, and
317	    /// left in place it makes the first block's index line unparseable.
318	    private static func normalized(_ raw: String) -> String {
319	        raw.replacingOccurrences(of: "\u{FEFF}", with: "")
320	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "\r\n", with: "\n")
321	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "\r", with: "\n")
322	    }
323	
324	    private static func isBlank(_ line: String) -> Bool {
325	        line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty
326	    }
327	
328	    private static func trimmed(_ text: String) -> String {
329	        text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
330	    }
331	
332	    // MARK: - Placement
333	
334	    /// Everything an import will do, computed against `project` and applied
335	    /// by nobody: the UI commits it through `ProjectDocument`, the agent
336	    /// through `AgentServer.editResult`.
337	    ///
338	    /// The whole of the placement is `CaptionLayout.place` — this is the
339	    /// SubRip half handing its cues over, and the file name being put back
340	    /// into the refusals so the alert and the tool's error string say which
341	    /// file they are about.
342	    ///
343	    /// `track` places on an existing track; absent, the captions get a new
344	    /// front-most track of their own, which is the only placement that can
345	    /// never be refused by the overlap rule.
346	    static func plan(for url: URL, in project: ReelProject, track: UInt32? = nil) throws -> Plan {
347	        let parsed = parse(try text(of: url))
348	        guard !parsed.cues.isEmpty else {
349	            throw CaptionError.noCues(url, parsed.problems)
350	        }
351	        let cues = parsed.cues.map {
352	            CaptionLayout.Cue(start: $0.start, end: $0.end, text: $0.text, tag: "line \($0.line)")
353	        }
354	        do {
355	            return try CaptionLayout.place(
356	                cues, problems: parsed.problems, in: project, track: track)
357	        } catch let error as CaptionLayout.LayoutError {
358	            switch error {
359	            case .noCues(let problems): throw CaptionError.noCues(url, problems)
360	            case .refused: throw CaptionError.refused(url)
361	            case .tooMany(let cues, let room):
362	                throw CaptionError.tooMany(url, cues: cues, room: room)
363	            }
364	        }
365	    }
366	}

372	extension EditorViewController {
373	
374	    /// The open panel, then the import. Both the panel's completion and the
375	    /// alert that follows it are OFF-EVENT, which is why the edit goes
376	    /// through `performGroupedEdit` (app/CLAUDE.md's undo pitfall).
377	    func importCaptionsCommand() {
378	        guard let document = document, let window = view.window else {
379	            NSSound.beep()
380	            return
381	        }
382	        let panel = NSOpenPanel()
383	        panel.allowsMultipleSelection = false
384	        panel.canChooseDirectories = false
385	        panel.allowedContentTypes = CaptionImporter.contentTypes
386	        panel.message = "Choose a SubRip (.srt) caption file."
387	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak self] response in
388	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
389	            self?.importCaptions(from: url, into: document, in: window)
390	        }
391	    }
392	
393	    private func importCaptions(from url: URL, into document: ProjectDocument, in window: NSWindow)
394	    {
395	        let plan: CaptionImporter.Plan
396	        do {
397	            // **The EDITED project, not the document.** A caption plan
398	            // measures a placement — the frame grid, the overlap trim, the
399	            // new front-most track — and road map 2's phase 9 addresses the
400	            // ops it produces to whatever nest is open. Reading the document
401	            // here and writing into the nest there is one gesture computing
402	            // against one container and landing in another, which is the
403	            // shape `SilenceDetector` and `AudioNormalize` were moved off
404	            // in the same phase. A producer reads the container it writes.
405	            plan = try CaptionImporter.plan(for: url, in: document.editedProject)
406	        } catch {
407	            let alert = NSAlert(error: error)
408	            alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
409	            return
410	        }
411	        document.performGroupedEdit("Import Captions", plan.ops)
412	        guard !plan.report.isEmpty else { return }
413	        let alert = NSAlert()
414	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
415	        alert.messageText =
416	            "Imported \(plan.clips) caption\(plan.clips == 1 ? "" : "s") from "
417	            + "“\(url.lastPathComponent)”."
418	        alert.informativeText = plan.report
419	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "OK")
420	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
421	    }
422	}

traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,

  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of

  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one

  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`

  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:

  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not

  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and

  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`
  (`person`, `foreground`), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground`, `CutoutProps` (`VideoProps.cutout` and

  write `VideoPatch.cutoutPart` carries — written under `cutout` only when `cutout` is nil,
  never decoded — so a Background, Edge or Feather row writes its own key alone, CO3),
  `RecipeCutoutMaskKind` (`media`, and `image`, drawn since CO10b from the
  picture's one mask, CO-107),
  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,
  `TransitionSnapshot`) and `TrackSnapshot.swift` (`TrackSnapshot`) are pure moves out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T11–T13). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name

  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted

  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`, +`Reverse`, +`Derived`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation
  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with the `ReelRefusal` (spec §11 CI-10), which
  the editor forwards to the inspector's refusal strip. Holds the SIX pieces of view state nothing persists —
  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the
  scope FIRST, since the selection clamp measures against whatever
  container the scope left. `selectedAction` (spec §11 CI-1) is nil or one
  action of the SINGLE selected clip; `+SelectedAction` holds its queries,
  its one deliberate writer `selectAction(_:)` (which stores nil for an id
  that is not `singleSelectedClip`'s) and the ENTRY rule
  `syncSelectedAction()`, run from `playhead`'s and `selection`'s `didSet`
  against `lastInsideAction`. The clamp re-reads `lastInsideAction` BEFORE
  its last line writes the playhead, so an edit, undo or redo under a
  stationary playhead never enters a span — keep those two lines above
  that write. `nestPath` is a
  PATH of (nest, clip) steps, not a nest id, because two clips can show one
  nest at two starts; `editedProject` is a STORED, memoised `rc_project_scoped`
  handle, and `project` still means the parent for save, export and
  consolidate. A range is cleared on every scope change: a pair of ticks means
  one thing inside a nest and another to an export. `+UndoGroup`:
  `inUndoGroupIfRegistered` runs a body with an undo group pending, and
  `registerUndo(restoring:actionName:)`'s first statement
  (`openPendingUndoGroup()`) opens it at the body's first registration, at the
  body's level and never while undoing or redoing; a body that registers
  nothing leaves undo and redo untouched (#167); `registerUndo` stays the one
  registrar. `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)` (#272) undoes the step that ended at
  `step` before committing, when `project` is still that handle, so a strip's
  off-knob double-click is one step. `cacheDirectory` calls `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` when it
  creates `cache/` — only if the package's date, read through a fresh `URL`
  before the create, is still `fileModificationDate`, so an outside change made before it is not absorbed — and that method re-reads the date through a fresh
  `URL`, because `fileURL` still holds the date it cached at open (#138).
  `+CacheSaves` is the `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)` override
  every save funnels through, bracketing it with the cache ledger's
  `saveBegan` / `saveEnded` (#115, #169).
  `+Import` is File ▸ Add Media… and every drop into an open project
  (`importMedia`, the probe chain and the one grouped commit), the opening
  read's probe (`probeForOpening`, a cancelled copy as `.userCancelled`), and the Media
  tab's Relink… and the missing-media sheet's body (`relinkMedia(_:)`: each
  file probed through `MediaImporter.probe`, one grouped "Relink Media" edit
  carrying each descriptor as `relink_media`'s `probe`, spec §11 #63, then

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

/// what the preview draws.
///
/// **Each box is remembered under its own key**, read when the row is built
/// and written by a CLICK (`lookChanged`) — never by Generate — and never by
/// the tool (R6-2 read across). An absent key is off, so a build that
/// remembered only a style opens with all three off.
///
/// **The note** shows whenever On this Mac is the engine and Dim is live (a
/// word style), ticked or not: the on-device engine's word ranges tile the
/// audio, so its words rarely carry the pause a dim waits for (W-13). It
/// wraps to two lines at the column's width, so the card is about two lines
/// taller while it shows.
extension TranscribeSheetController {

    /// The owner's sentence (spec §11 W-15).
    static let dimNote = "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI."

    /// The looks a run commits: each box ENABLED and on.

                            + "placed."),

                        .dim,
                        "The page fades to half its opacity in a pause of 0.25 s or more: writes "
                            + "word_style.pause_dim 0.5 on every page placed. On-device "
                            + "(engine apple) words rarely carry a pause that long, so it shows "
                            + "mostly with assemblyai."),

                        "type": "boolean",

                "Writes one text track out as a subtitle file — File ▸ Export Captions…. Every "
                    + "text clip on the track becomes one cue at the time it sits at, in the "
                    + "order they play. THE TRACK IS NEVER GUESSED: the default is the single "
                    + "track whose clips are ALL text clips, and with none or with more than "
                    + "one the call is refused and the candidates listed by id and name — "
                    + "writing the wrong track and reporting success is the failure this rule "
                    + "prevents. WebVTT escapes &, < and > where SubRip does not, so on text "
                    + "containing none of the three the two files differ only by the WEBVTT "
                    + "header, the missing index lines and a . where SubRip writes a , in the "
                    + "timestamps. A round trip back through import_captions returns every cue "
                    + "to the TICK it was written from, at every ordinary frame rate: a "
                    + "timestamp is rounded to the nearest millisecond, at most 300 ticks, and "
                    + "half a frame is 10,000 ticks even at 30 fps, so the snap on the way "
                    + "back in lands on the frame the cue left. What is not exact is the "
                    + "FILE: import_captions snaps every cue to the frame grid, so a source "

                    + "00:00:04,120 returns as 00:00:04,133 — and byte identity with the file "

**Pauses come from word gaps of 0.25 s plus sentence punctuation. The
silence detector is not consulted (W-7; orig §5c, §10.9).**
`SpeechTranscriber`'s word ranges TILE the audio: a 1.57 s real silence
showed as a 0.30 s gap, and a 1.13 s one as 0.06 s. So the literature's
0.4 s `breakGap` found nothing, and 0.25 s was chosen. W4a injected road map
4's detector pauses as forced breaks and got the same ten pages, because the
punctuation already broke there.

**Each engine has its own `lead`, applied once in `normalize` and never to
  is sooner. The pill appears on a page's first word; it never flies in from
  the page before.
- **A word takes at most 0.6 s to fill** (the owner's choice 4 (a)), because
  an on-device word's `end` is stretched over the silence after it. Known
  limits has both engines' behaviour.
- A pause dims only from 0.25 s, over 0.1 s each way; the depth is the key's
  value. **The dim is built as specified** (the owner's choice 7 (a)) though
  Mode off, thermal state nominal).
- **A fill follows a word's stored `end`, and the two engines store
  different ends** (issue batch B86 phase 1, spec §11 W-13). AssemblyAI's
  `end` is where the word was heard to end, so the fill keeps time with the
  voice and then stays full. The on-device engine's word ranges tile the
  audio (the 1.57 s silence stored as a 0.30 s gap, the 1.13 s one as
  0.06 s, above), so the last word before a pause is stored as lasting
  through most of it. A word therefore takes at most 0.6 s to fill
  (`WORD_FILL_MAX`, the owner's choice, a chosen number and not a measured
  one), which stops that crawl; its cost is that a word really spoken for
  longer than 0.6 s, with either engine, finishes its fill early.
- **On generated captions the dim is a page's tail, not a pause in
  mid-page** (B86 phase 1, W-13). Only a pause of 0.25 s or more dims, and
  the pager already ENDS a page at a 0.25 s pause (W-7) and takes it down at
  most 0.5 s later. So with AssemblyAI words a page that is followed by a
  pause fades for its last 0.25–0.5 s; with on-device words mostly nothing
  happens, because the stretched `end` leaves gaps under 0.25 s (0.06 s for
  the 1.13 s silence; the 1.57 s one left 0.30 s, so that page's last 0.3 s
  dims). The dim behaves as W-13 describes — down, then back before the next
  word — on a page timed by hand or by an agent. Trimming on-device word
  ends against the silence detector is not built.

docs/guide/assistant.md:123:**Cutting words.** Ask it to take out filler words and it finds them and cuts them in one step, but only in media that already have a cloud transcript made with filler words (by **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**). The assistant can't upload audio to make one, so in other media that search finds nothing and reports which media have no such transcript. The words it reads there still flag any filler they hold, but words not transcribed with filler words can leave fillers out. Ask it to remove a false start and it reads the clip's words and their times (from the media's cached transcript, or from this Mac's own speech recogniser, never the network), says which words it will cut, then cuts them as one undo step. docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:86:There is nothing to tune. Each run of consecutive fillers becomes one cut:

docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:89:- Its edges then snap inward to the frame grid, as Remove Silences does. A tiny filler can end up too short to cut.
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:90:- A filler is **left in whole**, never trimmed, when cutting it would reach into a word spoken in another clip on any unlocked track, into a nest clip, or into a transition. The sheet counts these: "2 fillers are left in: too short to cut, or cutting would reach another clip's word, a nest or a transition."
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:98:Filler words come only from an **AssemblyAI** transcript made with filler words. Transcription on your Mac doesn't report them reliably. This makes filler removal a cloud feature: you need an AssemblyAI API key, set in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,) under **Transcription**.
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:100:With no key, **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** is greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**; resting the pointer on it says "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The exception is a project where a file in scope already has a transcript made with filler words: that transcript is already paid for, so the command stays on and cuts its fillers without a key. Saving a key in Settings turns the command on at once.
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:102:Every AssemblyAI transcription Frame Job makes asks for filler words. Only files never transcribed in the cloud, or transcribed before filler words were requested, are listed in the sheet.
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:104:When a file in scope has no such transcript, the sheet lists it under "Filler words are found only in an AssemblyAI transcript made with filler words — transcription on this Mac does not report them. These files have none yet:". Each listed file gets a row with:
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:114:- It reuses that file's earlier transcription choices (language, speaker labels and vocabulary) and adds filler words. A file never transcribed before uses language detection, no speakers and no vocabulary.
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:115:- A file listed here that already has a caption transcript is uploaded again: that older transcript was made without filler words, so this is a second paid transcription.

app_defects.title: Windows-1252 and Latin-1 caption files are effectively never decoded as those encodings
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/CaptionImporter.swift:144 tries .utf16 before .windowsCP1252 and .isoLatin1, and Foundation's .utf16 accepts BOM-less bytes. I ran the same decode loop on a Windows-1252 SRT with accented letters at 64 lengths: all 64 decoded as UTF-16 CJK garbage with no '-->', so the import fails with 'No captions could be read'. A Latin-1 sample at two lengths did the same. The comment at CaptionImporter.swift:136-141 says the single-byte arms are reachable and that mojibake is the worst case. Little-endian UTF-16 with no BOM also decodes as garbage.

app_defects.title: export_captions catalog text says candidates are listed when there are none
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/AgentCatalog+Captions.swift:348-349 says 'with none or with more than one the call is refused and the candidates listed by id and name'. With none, CaptionExporter.swift:125-126 throws .noTextTrack, which reads 'No track holds only text clips, so there are no captions to write.' and lists nothing.

app_defects.title: A valid WebVTT file always reports its header as a malformed entry
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/CaptionImporter.swift:131 offers .text, and org.w3.webvtt conforms to public.text, so the open panel should admit .vtt (the type's conformance was checked; the panel itself was not opened). I ran the real parser (lines 156-330) on a sample: both cues imported, and the WEBVTT header, a STYLE block and a NOTE block each came back as 'no “-->” timing line in this entry'. A well-formed file therefore ends in the skipped-entries alert.
